title: Stance Comparison — Core Method
description: Mapping contradictions starts with stance: for each record's claims about a topic — supports, refutes, or neutral — extracted from its text. Two records with opposing stances on the same claim are a contradiction edge, recorded with the claim text and both positions. Stance extraction uses claim templates and negation detection rather than deep magic, keeping it auditable. Note the distinction: detection finds disagreements, but this tool maps them into a navigable structure of who-disagrees-with-whom about what. At ladder rank 1 this is the simple core: a single, self-contained application of the method.
provenance: JAH Databases archive-intelligence tools program, lane T2a — public methods from established computer-science practice.

title: Contradiction Graph Edges — Core Method
description: Each contradiction becomes an edge in a graph whose nodes are records and whose edges carry the disputed claim plus a severity. Severity weighs the claim's importance and the records' authority — a disagreement between landmark studies matters more than one between stubs. The graph is queryable: 'show everything contradicting record X', 'find the most disputed claim'. Edges turn scattered disagreements into a map of the archive's fault lines. At ladder rank 1 this is the simple core: a single, self-contained application of the method.

title: Disagreement Clustering — Core Method
description: Contradiction edges cluster into controversy groups: sets of records mutually disagreeing about a shared topic. The mapper finds connected components in the contradiction graph, and each component becomes one controversy with its member records and disputed claims. Large components mark the archive's hot-button topics; isolated edges are one-off disputes. Clustering tells researchers where the real debates live instead of making them assemble the picture edge by edge. At ladder rank 1 this is the simple core: a single, self-contained application of the method.

title: Two-Sided Evidence Linking — Core Method
description: A contradiction edge is more useful when both sides' evidence is attached: the mapper links each disputing record to the sources, data, and reasoning it cites. Evidence links let a reader judge the disagreement on its merits instead of taking sides blindly. The links also reveal patterns — one side citing primary data, the other citing reviews — that characterize the controversy's nature. Mapping means connecting the disagreement to its foundations, not just noting that it exists. At ladder rank 1 this is the simple core: a single, self-contained application of the method.

title: Resolution Pathing — Core Method
description: The mapper does not resolve contradictions — it maps paths toward resolution: which experiment would discriminate, which newer record supersedes, which authority adjudicates. Each suggested path names the missing evidence and where it might be found, turning a deadlocked disagreement into a research plan. Paths are ranked by feasibility, cheapest test first. A contradiction map with resolution paths is a research agenda generated from the archive's own disagreements. At ladder rank 1 this is the simple core: a single, self-contained application of the method.
